newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler says needs 15 bln for refinance.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says needs 15 bln for refinance.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG, Germany's largest industrial group, on Wednesday said it will need to raise 15 billion marks ($9.8 billion) in 1997, largely to help refinance its leasing and sales operations.
Daimler said it plans to tap the capital markets for the funds and said that of the 15 billion marks total, 13 billion marks will be used for renewing debt and two billion marks will be for new use.
Daimler-Benz chief financial officer Manfred Gentz told a group of bankers that the group's 1997 financing for its industrial operations would largely be covered by the cash flow.
"But we expect to need refinancings totalling 15 billion marks, largely for the leasing and sales operations, and this will be largely covered by raising funds on the capital market," he added.
Daimler-Benz released a summary statement of Gentz's speech text ahead of delivery.
In 1998, Gentz predicted Daimler will need 18 billion marks for refinancing with 14 billion marks going to renewing debt and four billion for new uses.
